title: The Minimum Number of Measurements for Almost-Everywhere Complex Phase Retrieval
summary: Let $d\geq 2$ and let $\bf{f}_1,\ldots,\bf{f}_m\in\mathbb C^d$. We prove that if $m\leq 2d-1$, then the intensity measurement map \[ \bf{x}\longmapsto \bigl( |\langle \bf{x},\bf{f}_1\rangle|^2, \ldots, |\langle \bf{x},\bf{f}_m\rangle|^2 \bigr) \] fails to recover almost every signal in $\mathbb C^d$ uniquely up to a global phase factor. Combined with the known generic sufficiency of $2d$ measurements, our result establishes that the minimum number of measurements required for almost-everywhere phase retrieval in $\mathbb C^d$ is exactly $2d$. This resolves an open problem in phase retrieval…
